collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A homesick villager sneaks home early from a long walk and meets a friend on the path: pretend not to notice, or say you're glad.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) set off yesterday morning for a long walk along the coast, with a full bag and a big farewell. (subject.He/she) is now walking back into the village, a day and a half early, trying to look casual. (subject.He/she) missed home. Badly. On the first night. (subject.He/she) is hoping nobody will notice. (friend) is standing right in the middle of the path.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "You're back!" says (friend). "Good. It's been too quiet." (subject) braces for teasing, and none comes. (subject.He/she) explains, a bit sheepishly, about missing home. (friend) shrugs. "Sounds like you found out something about yourself." (subject) thinks about that. Maybe (subject.he/she) did. (subject.He/she) might try the walk again someday. Or not.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "Oh, hello," says (friend), as if (subject) has just popped out for a moment. "Good timing. Stew's nearly ready." (subject) is so grateful (subject.he/she) could cry. They eat together and talk about everything except the walk. Much later, (subject) admits, "I missed home." "I know," says (friend). "Have some more stew."
